label: E2 Finance
situation: Tokenised-market data arrived through changing on-chain pools, token contracts and reference sources that did not form a reliable common catalogue by themselves.
contribution: Eirik built and operates a TypeScript and Next.js market-intelligence and wallet-controlled transaction system. He created a canonical registry of 194 verified stock-token assets and 1,113 pools, normalised token, pool, counterparty and protocol relationships, and added executable quote analysis, reference-price reconciliation, provenance and explicit data-quality states.
outcome: The live data layer produces a continuously refreshed, decision-ready view of pool state, reference integrity and executable depth across the verified market catalogue.
boundary: The system and data scale are established; customer adoption, revenue and realised trading performance are not.

label: Opportunity Engine
situation: Job records from thousands of employer boards change, duplicate, disappear and expose inconsistent identifiers and fields, making manual review and stable application tracking difficult.
contribution: Eirik built and operates an opportunity-intelligence system with deterministic ingestion, canonicalisation, deduplication, freshness and geography controls, persisted SQLite state, source-health monitoring, ranked decision queues, dashboards and bounded LLM-assisted evaluation.
outcome: A production refresh on 8 September 2026 completed 14,992 board requests, ingested 8,184 new jobs and updated 59,490 changed records without Brave or LLM calls in the high-volume discovery path.
boundary: This is a large operational search universe, not a claim of complete internet-wide coverage or fully autonomous application submission.

label: Eirik.co.uk AI interface
situation: A public career interface needed to answer open-ended questions accurately without sending an entire private career corpus or allowing unsupported claims.
contribution: Eirik built and operates a retrieval-grounded LLM application using Next.js, direct model APIs and PostgreSQL conversation state, with deterministic evidence selection, streaming responses, bounded history, usage telemetry, rate limits and prompt controls.
outcome: The system is live and its evidence selections and token usage are recorded for evaluation and improvement.
boundary: Describe this as deterministic retrieval-grounded generation, not vector search or embedding-based retrieval.

label: Bittensor credit infrastructure
situation: Bittensor subnet assets needed a credible route into isolated credit markets despite unusual collateral, liquidity, oracle and liquidation risks.
contribution: Eirik led product and commercial development for a Bittensor credit protocol built on Morpho isolated lending markets. He owned the product architecture, user flows, requirements, roadmap, collateral onboarding, loan-to-value and debt-cap methodology, liquidity analysis, oracle and liquidation design, financial model and partner work while coordinating an eight-person development team and external technical lead.
outcome: Substantial funded development reached functional implementation and serious strategic discussions before the underlying ecosystem changed.
boundary: Eirik did not personally write every component, and the work did not produce a scaled institutional launch, completed external fundraise or scaled revenue.

label: Bittensor quantitative research system
situation: Rapidly changing subnet markets required a comparable historical panel that handled identity and lifecycle changes before predictive signals could be tested honestly.
contribution: Eirik built a canonical market dataset and repeatable refresh pipeline spanning price, liquidity, flows, incentives and market structure, then built feature engineering, regularised and tree-based models, walk-forward validation, frozen holdouts, portfolio simulation, regime analysis and reproducible automated research campaigns.
outcome: The infrastructure created a rigorous, repeatable process for searching for potential alpha and rejecting weak results.
boundary: The working research system is established; proven profitable or deployable alpha is not.

label: Bittensor compute and inference work
situation: Decentralised compute and inference markets must aggregate independent suppliers while making service quality, verification, utilisation and incentives commercially workable.
contribution: Eirik worked on product, market and commercial questions including node and executor economics, supply aggregation, verification, incentives, product positioning, competitive research, partnerships and go-to-market.
outcome: This formed part of sustained paid professional work within the Bittensor ecosystem alongside venture and independent work.
boundary: Do not claim formal employment by Opentensor or the Bittensor Foundation, or that Eirik personally operated every node or built an entire network.

label: DUSD Markets
situation: A live Solana launchpad and market workflow required connected transaction, indexing, market-state, settlement, fee-routing and recovery processes rather than a purely presentational web interface.
contribution: Eirik built and operates the TypeScript, Express and SQLite system across test and mainnet services, including stateful transaction workflows, indexing, settlement records, monitoring and Linux deployment.
outcome: On 8 September 2026 production had recorded 1,015 platform trades, 112 external-market trades, 609 market snapshots and 429 completed settlement records.
boundary: Wallets are not verified users; do not claim custody, audited contracts, revenue or profitability.

label: dusd.fun analytics and automation
situation: A community-run Solana token with fee-funded buy-and-burn mechanics needed understandable live supply, burn, liquidity and transaction evidence plus reliable unattended automation.
contribution: Eirik independently designed, built, deployed and operates the Next.js and TypeScript analytics product and its guarded Node.js transaction automation, including APIs, on-chain indexing, charts, calculators, simulation, signing, recovery, monitoring and VPS operations.
outcome: The product is live, actively maintained and receives around 300 unique daily visitors.
boundary: The underlying asset is a community or meme token; Eirik built the surrounding product and did not found the token or wider community.

label: KPMG Financial Services Assurance
situation: Banks, asset managers, hedge funds, fund administrators and fintechs needed assurance over how transactions, financial information and technology-enabled processes moved through operational systems and reporting.
contribution: Eirik owned client workstreams analysing financial workflows, reconciliations, data interfaces, exceptions, downstream reporting, access and change controls and evidence across cloud-hosted delivery environments, communicating conclusions to senior client and internal stakeholders.
outcome: This provides nearly two years of regulated financial-services delivery and direct evidence of structured client ownership and cross-functional collaboration.
boundary: He assessed systems and their control environments; he did not architect or operate Kubernetes, CI/CD or GitOps platforms as an infrastructure engineer.

label: One Click Labs
situation: DeFi yield and market data was fragmented across DeFiLlama and protocol APIs, with inconsistent formats, rapidly changing APYs, incomplete history and economically different products that could not be compared safely from headline yield alone.
contribution: Eirik developed Python, SQL and Excel workflows for ingestion, cleaning, normalisation, validation, exception handling, backtesting, portfolio optimisation, risk analysis and performance attribution, then translated findings into product, capital-allocation and commercial recommendations for the founder.
outcome: The resulting data and analytical layer supported live investment analysis and a comparable portfolio decision framework.
boundary: The company later evolved into Yield Network; do not attribute that later product's current operation or results to Eirik.

label: Gartner Nordic Market
situation: Nordic emerging-technology companies required commercial discovery and market analysis around enterprise technology needs.
contribution: Eirik worked across prospecting, discovery, market research and client communication.
outcome: The work generated more than $150,000 in potential contract value.
boundary: This was a short internship and potential contract value, not closed revenue or long-tenure enterprise-sales leadership.

contribution: He completed a BSc in Accounting and Finance at Warwick with Upper Second-Class Honours at 69%, received a Future Leaders Scholarship and completed 12 of 15 ICAEW ACA examinations.
